To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the enhanced access of fearful faces to consciousness is due to their high effective contrast.
fearful faces have a higher effective contrast than other facial expressions and that the effective contrast of a face determines its likelihood of being perceived consciously.
the fearful expression has a sensory advantage in competition for awareness.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how we become aware of the world.
the mechanisms that underlie conscious awareness.
the relationship between the physical properties of visual stimuli and the mechanisms that determine which signals are promoted to conscious perception.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
fear advantage is a byproduct of the evolution of the human visual system and not a dedicated mechanism that evolved to promote threat related signals to consciousness.
fear is not a special case of visual awareness, and that the fear advantage is a byproduct of general mechanisms.
the fearful face has a sensory advantage in a competition for awareness.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
fearful faces are not privileged, but are simply more salient than other facial expressions.
the fear advantage is a sensory advantage.

the fearful face advantage is not a consequence of a dedicated threat processing pathway but is rather a consequence of an evolutionarily molded facial expression that exploits our general purpose sensory systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sensory advantages of fearful faces can be explained without assuming the existence of specialized mechanisms that promote the processing of threatening signals to awareness.
the fear advantage is not a special case of the more general phenomenon that the most salient stimuli are preferentially promoted to awareness.
the fear advantage is not an exception, but a consequence of general mechanisms that govern the competition for awareness.
